title: Pissaladière
subtitle: Provençal onion, anchovy, and olive flatbread
excerpt: The great Niçoise tart: a thick, crisp base of olive oil dough topped with a mass of slow-cooked melted onions, a criss-cross lattice of anchovy fillets, and black olives. Nothing like pizza; something altogether more ancient and satisfying.

recipe.sourceNotes: Pissaladière is the signature flatbread of Nice in the Alpes-Maritimes region of France, and takes its name from pissalat, a Niçoise condiment made from fermented anchovies and sardines (similar to garum in the ancient Roman culinary tradition, which was heavily practised in the area). The dish is related to pizza in that both are flatbreads from the Mediterranean rim, but pissaladière has a thicker, more focaccia-like base and the topping of slow-cooked onions, anchovies, and olives has no tomato sauce. The onions must be cooked for at least 45 minutes until completely soft and sweet; any remaining sharpness or moisture will prevent the tart from having its characteristic silky texture.

content.text: Cook the onions very slowly for at least 45 minutes over the lowest possible heat with the lid on; they must melt to a pale, sweet, almost jam-like consistency with no browning. Any caramelisation changes the flavour and the colour. The anchovies melt into the onions during baking; their saltiness is the seasoning for the whole tart.

items.preparation: 4 tbsp for the dough; rest for the onions and topping

content.text: Make the dough: dissolve the yeast in 180 ml warm water. Mix with the flour, 4 tablespoons of olive oil, and a pinch of salt. Knead for 8 minutes until smooth. Cover and leave to rise for 1 hour.

Cook the onions with the remaining olive oil, thyme, bay, and a pinch of salt over the lowest heat with the lid on for 45 to 60 minutes, stirring occasionally, until completely soft and pale. Remove the bay leaves. Season.

Heat the oven to 220°C / fan 200°C / gas 7. Press the risen dough onto an oiled baking tray into a rectangle about 1 cm thick. Spread the melted onions over evenly. Arrange the anchovy fillets in a diagonal lattice pattern across the top. Press an olive into each diamond of the lattice. Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until the base is golden and crisp. Serve warm or at room temperature.
